doc_friction.issue: It sends a venture run to `node platform/pages/venture-preflight.mjs <slug>` only before the merge, so a post's front-matter limits (description <= 160, seo_title <= 70) are found at the end of the run, after a 5-minute preflight. A one-line checker for just the changed posts, named where the post is written, would catch it in seconds; here it cost a whole preflight round.

The row it tells you to take ('Start here: row 5, photo-editing') is picked before claim_check.py runs, and claim_check then told me another session had claimed the same venture 1 minute earlier (PR #15457). allocate.py already reads open PRs for its '[older open PRs]' notes, so the picker could skip a venture with a PR opened in the last few minutes rather than sending two sessions to the same row.

Its post front-matter check reports one failure at a time and only after the other steps, so two 5-minute preflight rounds were spent on two limits of the same new post; and its 'site tests failed' step reported a post broken on main (PR #15454's Bulgaria post, title 116 and description 164 characters) with no hint which post, so the fix had to be found by rerunning promptctl validate.

'Long commands' says to start anything over 120 s with run_in_background, but says nothing about the container restarting under a long job. Three restarts here killed every background job with no output flushed (the redirect file was truncated mid-line), which reads like a hang rather than a kill: `uptime` showing 'up 1 min' is the only tell. Worth a line: check uptime before re-running, and prefer the narrowest check that fits in a few minutes.

goal: A measured speed-up in the raw read with byte-identical sensels, on both the numpy and the pure-Python install.
notes: Landed: tiles decoded from a lossless-JPEG DNG are now placed into the sensor plane on the thread that decoded them, as one 2-D numpy copy, instead of row-by-row array rebuilds on the calling thread after the pool (src/shootflow/raw_develop.py: _blit, _place_chunks, _decode_chunks(sink=)). Measured on the Pixel 3 XL pixel3.dng (MIT, tinydng, downloaded at check time), 4 CPUs, 10 repetitions a cell, old and new alternated three times: with numpy at 4 threads the median read goes 0.121-0.166 s to 0.089-0.136 s (1.3-1.4x in paired runs); 1 thread and a no-numpy Python unchanged within noise. Sensel SHA-256 7304e29f5ddae78c (first 16 hex) before and after, at 1/2/4 threads with numpy on and off: the same hash that matched LibRaw 0.22.2 sensel-for-sensel. First version was SLOWER without numpy because _blit_numpy() retried a failing `import numpy` per tile (192 full sys.path searches) and because the GIL-held row copy does not belong on the pool; both fixed (import cached, pure path placed on the calling thread). Verification run here: `python3 platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py photo-editing` ok in 153.7 s (1 suite, 0 failed), and `node platform/pages/venture-preflight.mjs photo-editing` (first run failed only on this run's new post's front matter, fixed, rerun). Also updated: README section, llms.txt timing, flagships.yaml `next:` (next on speed is now parse_raw's double plane allocation and C prediction for point-transform scans). Also fixed, outside the venture: docs/posts/2026-11-13-bulgaria-e-invoicing-draft-still-a-draft.md (landed on main in PR #15454) had a 116-character title and a 164-character description, which failed the repository-wide post front-matter tests and so failed this venture's preflight; trimmed both, and platform/pages site tests (56) now pass. Re-verified after the restarts, on the tree merged with origin/main: run_venture_tests.py photo-editing ok 158.7 s (0 failed) and platform/pages site tests 56/56. The merge with main conflicted only on docs/posts/2026-11-13-bulgaria-e-invoicing-draft-still-a-draft.md, where another session had trimmed the same over-length title; kept main's wording (109/62/155 characters).
